rows.name: Merck & Co.
rows.thesis: Large pharma at a reasonable valuation, with a new-drug pipeline building to offset Keytruda's patent expiry, and the stock is above its 200-day average.
rows.risks: Revenue loss after Keytruda's patent expiry, and the upcoming quarterly report.

rows.name: Targa Resources
rows.thesis: A fee-based pipeline and natural-gas-liquids network with rising volumes from the Permian basin; the stock is at a new high.
rows.risks: Energy concentration and lower drilling activity if commodity prices fall.

rows.name: Nucor
rows.thesis: Steel prices are supported by tariffs and rising US demand, and the stock is up 14% in a month to near its high.
rows.risks: Steel prices peaking or tariff policy changes.

rows.name: CrowdStrike
rows.thesis: The leading endpoint-security platform, with fast growth in recurring revenue and strong momentum (+85% over 12 months, 50% above its 200-day average).
rows.risks: A very high valuation, which this week's Fortinet sell-off shows the market is punishing in security stocks.

rows.name: Marathon Petroleum
rows.thesis: Refining margins are very high, and the company returns a lot of capital to shareholders through buybacks, backed by strong cash flow.
rows.risks: Refining margins could fall back to normal levels from their current peak.

rows.name: NetApp
rows.thesis: Demand for data storage driven by AI and a shift toward all-flash systems are lifting margins, with strong momentum.
rows.risks: Hardware-stock sentiment is turning, as STX and DELL have already pulled back.

rows.name: Illumina, Inc.
rows.thesis: A recovery in genetic-sequencing demand and better profit margins are driving earnings up; the stock is within 1.3% of its high.
rows.risks: Competition from cheaper sequencing rivals and possible China or tariff headlines.

rows.name: DuPont
rows.thesis: Since its split into separate companies, the remaining DuPont is a more focused electronics and industrial materials business, with strong price momentum near its highs.
rows.risks: A cyclical slowdown in industrial and electronics demand.

rows.name: Viatris
rows.thesis: A cheap generic-drug maker that is paying down debt and buying back shares, with steady momentum at its highs.
rows.risks: Price erosion in generic drugs and manufacturing compliance problems at its plants.

rows.name: Valero Energy
rows.thesis: Q3 EPS of $23.90 at near-record refinery use; the 10% weekly drop looks like profit-taking, not a broken thesis.
rows.risks: Refining margins normalizing, and overlap with MPC.

rows.name: Keysight Technologies
rows.thesis: Its testing and measurement equipment benefits from spending on AI data centers, 6G wireless and defense, and the stock is still above its 200-day average.
rows.risks: Momentum is fading (-6.8% this month, only 5.7% above the 200-day average), so a deeper slide would trigger a review.

rows.name: Fortinet
rows.thesis: Q3 beat with billings up 29%, and full-year guidance was raised for the third time this year; the 26% drop looks like a valuation reset, not a change in the business.
rows.risks: The firewall upgrade wave may be peaking, and stocks often keep drifting lower for weeks after a gap down on earnings.

rows.name: Morgan Stanley
rows.thesis: A steady fee-based wealth-management business, plus a recovery in investment banking deal activity.
rows.risks: The stock is below its 200-day average and 17% under its high; weak markets would hurt its fee income.
